correctness.rationale: The tame involution has genus-two quotient w^2=(t^3-a)^2-4 and Prym dimension two. A basis of anti-invariant holomorphic differentials dx/y^2 and x^2 dx/y^2 is killed by the Cartier operator: in F_5[a,x], coefficients [x^4]f^3 and [x^14]f^3, [x^4]f, and [x^4]x^2f all vanish. Thus Prym a-number is 2, which in dimension 2 implies superspeciality. The plus-block coefficients a and a(a^2-4), nonzero for a != 0 and a^2 !=4, give stable rank 2 and the stated source/quotient p-rank; quotient Hasse-Witt polynomial coefficients were checked independently. The squarefreeness and tameness exclusions are essential.
residual_risks: Superspecial means unpolarized isomorphism over the algebraic closure; no field descent, polarization or uniform classification of all Prym surfaces follows.
The a-number-to-superspecial equivalence is used as a standard dimension-two theorem, not independently reproved.
